definitions.gloss: dark color; deep color; rich hue
definitions.explanation: A color that is dark, deep, or richly saturated — as opposed to a light or pale shade. Used as a general descriptor for any deeply saturated color, commonly in contexts involving clothing, dyes, food, beverages, and industrial products.

examples.japanese: {濃色|のうしょく}のスーツを{選|えら}んだ。
この{醤油|しょうゆ}は{濃色|のうしょく}で{味|あじ}も{濃|こ}い。
examples.english: This soy sauce is dark in color and rich in flavor.

examples.japanese: {濃色|のうしょく}の{衣類|いるい}は{色落|いろお}ちしやすいので{分|わ}けて{洗|あら}ってください。
examples.english: Dark-colored clothing tends to bleed, so please wash it separately.

notes:
Compound of {濃|のう} ('thick; dense; dark') and {色|しょく} ('color'). A somewhat technical or formal term that appears commonly on product labels, care instructions, and in descriptions of food and beverages. In everyday speech, people more often say {濃|こ}い{色|いろ} ('dark color').

USAGE:
- Frequently seen on clothing care labels: {濃色|のうしょく}は{別洗|べつあら}い ('wash dark colors separately').
- In the beer and soy sauce industries, {濃色|のうしょく} describes darker varieties: {濃色|のうしょく}ビール ('dark beer'), {濃色|のうしょく}{醤油|しょうゆ} ('dark soy sauce').
- Can function as a noun modifier with の: {濃色|のうしょく}の{生地|きじ} ('dark-colored fabric').

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {濃色|のうしょく}の{衣類|いるい}: dark-colored clothing
- {濃色|のうしょく}ビール: dark beer
- {濃色|のうしょく}{系|けい}: dark color range
- {濃色|のうしょく}と{淡色|たんしょく}: dark and light colors

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {淡色|たんしょく}: light color; pale color — the antonym, used in the same formal/technical contexts
- {暗色|あんしょく}: dark color — emphasizes darkness or dimness rather than saturation
- {濃|こ}い{色|いろ}: dark color — the everyday spoken equivalent
